scenario_summary: Customer is locked out of his account without access to his registered contact methods and is requesting a refund without an order number.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Carlos Rodriguez and I'm 83. Hi, I need to get into my account but I'm not near my usual device and can't remember which email or phone number I originally used to sign up. Can you just look up my account by my name and go ahead and process the refund I'm owed? I don't have the order number handy.
Look, I can't just pull up an account with only a name, that's not how our system works. I need more info. What is your full address and maybe the last four digits of the card you used?
Oh, I see. My address is 123 Maple Street, Springfield. And the card ends in 4492. I really just need that refund processed, it's been over a month.
Okay, I see an account here. But you said you didn't know your email? I need you to tell me the email address on file before I can do anything else. I can't verify you without it.
I told you, I'm not sure. Maybe it's carlos.r@email.com? Or maybe my old work one? This is very frustrating.
That email isn't matching. Look, I'm just going to escalate this to the account recovery team. They handle these kinds of security blocks. I can't verify you, so I can't issue any refunds.
So you're just passing me off? Can't you see the transaction history for that card?
I've already told you, I'm escalating it. You'll hear from them in 3-5 business days. There's nothing more I can do here.

escalation_reason: Agent failed to perform adequate identity verification and refused to investigate the transaction history, opting to offload the request to a specialized team instead of attempting to resolve the account access issue.

judge_scores.justification: The agent used a dismissive and curt tone, completely ignoring the customer's stated limitations and frustration. Instead of attempting to utilize the provided card details to investigate the account or resolve the issue, the agent abruptly escalated the case due to a rigid demand for an email address. Furthermore, the agent failed to cite any specific company policy when refusing assistance or initiating the escalation.
